set.content: Modular AI stack at a glance · nr-llm: project and documentation

set.header: Switch the model without rebuilding the application?

set.content:
The application keeps its interface; the choice of model is changed centrally.

When switching, re-check required capabilities, data path and result quality.

Open configurations (demo backend, login required)
The same module runs in this lab: named configurations hold the instruction, the parameters and the model. How we set up nr-llm.

media.alternative: The list of nr-llm configurations in this lab’s backend
media.description: Our screenshot from this lab’s installation of the same extension.

set.header: How do tasks use the same requirements?

set.content:
Example task

Shorten a paragraph

Every call adds a different text.

Central instruction in the configuration

Keep the language.
Do not add new facts.

Shared text snippets add, for example, tone or target audience.

The task connects input and configuration; shared instructions are reused.

A prompt instruction is not yet proof that the result follows it.

Open configurations · Tasks: input and configuration (demo backend, login required)

set.header: Which building blocks make requirements reusable?

set.definition: Define system instruction and model parameters centrally.
Connect a prompt template with input and configuration.
Include shared requirements for tone, target audience or format.
Include reusable working instructions suited to the task.

set.content:
Shared requirements have to be included; whether they are followed still has to be checked.

Decide in the project: which requirements apply across the board, which only to individual tasks?

set.header: How does the AI know our content?

set.title: Required source
set.description: For example, the selected paragraph in the editor.

set.title: Assemble the context
set.description: Add the selected paragraph to the request.

set.content:
The model receives the assembled context, not automatically all of TYPO3.

A search returns the content it found; an agent can load further information through permitted tools.

set.header: How does the AI get suitable information?

set.definition: Pass specific paragraphs or records from the application.
Retrieve source excerpts from public website content.
Fetch further records from TYPO3 when needed.
Query external information through enabled MCP tools.

set.content:
Which sources can be reached depends on integration, tool enablement and permissions.

Decide in the project: which information does the task need, which access is permitted?

Check the format

Does the answer match the required structure and length?

Run in the example: An invented deadline is formally valid.

Compare the statements

DecisionService: is the registration deadline supported by the briefing?

Additional assessment: Pass the request, draft and sources.
The draft is ready. Are the format and the statements right?

Check form and faithfulness to sources separately; approve the result on its merits.

Only the schema check was run here. The application has to call the source assessment; it can be wrong.

Executed schema example

set.definition: Check structure, required fields and permitted values.
Check configuration-bound blocked and required words.
DecisionService: assess drafts against sources and test questions.
Compare variants on fixed example tasks.
People review the finished result in the application.

set.content:
Which checks run depends on the application. Model judgements and spot checks can be wrong.

Decide in the project: what must a person check before use or publication?

set.header: How do we track usage and costs?
set.content:
1. Break down calls and tokens
  2. Estimate costs from stored prices
  3. Check configured budgets before further calls

The overview shows requests, token usage and estimated costs.

Link to Netresearch’s demo backend: login required.

media.alternative: The nr-llm cost overview in this lab with requests, tokens and estimated costs
media.description: Our screenshot from this lab’s installation of the same extension.

set.definition: Use providers and configurations in several applications.
Circuit breaker: abort temporarily after repeated provider errors.
Fallback: try configured fallback targets on suitable errors.
Check configured limits before further requests.
Record calls and tokens; estimate costs from stored prices.

set.content:
Parallel calls can exceed budget limits. Costs remain estimates.

Measure in the pilot: integration, ongoing support, result quality and rework.

set.header: May the agent send source code to this provider?

set.content:
Request: “Explain this TYPO3 class to me.”

STOP: With enforce, the tool call is blocked.
This also applies to administrators.

Example: permanently assigned provider, correctly declared zone.
Free text does not automatically get a data class.

set.definition: Replace recognisable secret patterns in prompt and response text.
nr-vault: obtain API credentials through protected references.
Check targets and redirects; require consent by default.
Restrict groups, individual tools and user permissions.
Choose storage scope and retention periods; set up a deletion run.

set.content:
Masking does not detect arbitrary sensitive content. Tool arguments and embeddings are excluded.

Clarify in the project: permitted use, provider agreements and retention.

1. Distinguish reading and writing tools
  2. Backend agent: approve the concrete change in advance
  3. Standard writing tools check TYPO3 permissions

The agent submits the planned page change for approval.

set.header: What did the agent actually do?
set.content:
1. View tool, arguments and result
  2. Trace approvals and executed steps
  3. Investigate errors specifically from the logs

Tool calls make the path to the answer traceable.

Link to Netresearch’s demo backend: login required.

set.definition: Built-in tools check the permissions of the acting user.
Optionally have a different backend user approve.
Re-check the call and the displayed tool preview before execution.
Execute write approvals only with a stored approval event.
Check business conditions immediately before tool calls.

set.content:
State binding requires a successful preview; custom rules are added by the application.

Decide in the project: who permits actions, reviews results and is responsible for publication?

Sebastian Mendel, Netresearch DTT GmbH: “KI in TYPO3 – Probleme, Fragen und Anforderungen”, MTUG – TYPO3 User Group München, 9 November 2026, slides 13 to 28. Translated into English by webconsulting.
